subject: Renewal negotiation — Dedicated pool increase & burst overflow options
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@procurecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: account-exec@nimbus-ai.com; procurement@nimbus-ai.com
Date: 2026-02-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal thoughts — pool increase + burst behavior

Marissa,

Thanks for the renewal paperwork. We're generally happy with the dedicated pool proposal, but a couple things came up from our infra team:

- We need an additional reserved capacity band of GPUs during the renewal term — roughly +8 A100-equivalent GPUs on top of our current 32-GPU reserved pool.
- We also need clarity on how burst traffic is handled. During last quarter's spike we spilled over to on-demand and the cost was unpredictable; we'd like a written overflow policy (preferably with a hard cap or a committed burst buffer) so we can budget.

Can Redwood offer either a firm burst buffer (committed extra capacity) or a predictable overflow pricing model with a hard limit? If a committed burst pool is available, what's the incremental monthly commitment and SLA for throughput guarantees?

Appreciate a quick sketch — procurement wants this locked by renewal next week.

Best,
Linda Park
Head of Procurement
ProcureCorp

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@procurecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts — pool increase + burst behavior

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear ask. Short version up front: we can accommodate both paths you described.

Options we can propose quickly:
1) Committed burst buffer: +8 A100 equiv, reserved and priced as a smaller "burst pool" attached to your Dedicated instance. This comes with a 99.9% throughput SLA for steady-state and a documented fallback policy if hardware-level contention occurs. Incremental commit: $26,000/month (12-month term).

2) Predictable overflow pricing: keep your current reserved pool size (32 GPUs) and allow on-demand spillover up to +20% of your reserved capacity at a pre-negotiated per-hour rate. We can also tier that pricing so the first 10% overflow is at X, 10-20% at Y. We can optionally set a hard upper cap so your costs never exceed a defined budget.

I'll attach an updated term sheet and the capacity pricing matrix for numerical detail. Rishi/Neha are looped for SLO and implementation notes.

Next steps: Linda, if you confirm which option you prefer (committed buffer vs overflow + cap), we can finalize the term sheet and send to DocuSign. If you want the committed buffer, we can also propose a 12-month hidden ramp to avoid immediate capacity rebalancing events.

—Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: renewal_term_sheet_v2.pdf, capacity_pricing.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@procurecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-04T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts — pool increase + burst behavior

Linda — quick technical context from infra: 

- Committed burst pool (+8 GPUs): we can attach as a logically reserved sub-pool. Latency/throughput guarantees apply when requests route to reserved nodes; if you use more than reserved+burst, we will route to on-demand with standard best-effort latencies.
- Overflow behavior with hard cap: our platform supports a spend-cap guard that will prevent any new on-demand instances beyond a configured threshold. If you hit the cap, requests will receive 429s or be queued depending on route policy. We can also provide a graceful degradation policy (lower max tokens per request) instead of outright 429s.
- Instrumentation: we'll expose per-route token/sec and burst counters in the Console and can push daily usage exports to your S3.

Tradeoffs to highlight: committed burst gives you predictable performance and fewer 429s, but increases committed cost. Overflow + hard cap gives budget certainty but can result in degraded user experience during extreme spikes.

Happy to run a simulated spike test if you want verification before signing.

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect

Thanks — helpful. Procurement preference is: 1) keep predictable costs, 2) avoid unexpected 429s in production. We'd prefer the committed burst buffer if there's an option to discount it if we sign a 24-month renewal. Also need to confirm whether committed burst capacity counts toward our reserved commitment (i.e., is it part of the committed baseline for renewals) or is it billed and tracked separately.

Can you send a comparison table (12-month vs 24-month pricing, and whether burst pool is additive to reserved commitment)? Also need the specific wording for the burst overflow policy to include in our contract redline.

-Linda

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@procurecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-09T14:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts — pool increase & burst policy wording

Linda — attached is a concise comparison table and a suggested contract clause you can drop into your redline. Key points:

- Committed burst pool is additive to the reserved baseline and billed as a separate reserved line item (so it does not reduce the core baseline commitment). However, for 24-month commitments we can offer a 12% effective discount on the burst line.
- 12-month term: +8 GPUs (A100 equiv) = $26,000/mo; 24-month term: $23,000/mo (12% discount), annual invoicing options available.
- Burst overflow policy (suggested wording): "Customer will be allocated a committed burst pool of 8 GPU-equivalents. If Customer traffic exceeds (reserved + committed burst), Redwood may route excess requests to on-demand capacity at published overflow rates. Redwood will not route requests to on-demand capacity beyond a configured spend cap unless authorized in writing by the Customer. In the event the spend cap is reached, Redwood will apply the agreed graceful degradation policy (reduce max tokens per request) before returning 429s. Redwood will provide daily burst usage metrics and a monthly report."

If that looks good, we'll update the term sheet and send for e-signature. Happy to add a clause that the burst pool counts toward the dedicated capacity SLA for throughput guarantees while it is active.

—Marissa
Attachments: renewal_term_sheet_v2.pdf, capacity_pricing.xlsx
